title: Fish sandwich, fried, on white bun

content.title: About
content.content: A fried fish sandwich served on a soft white bun. It contains a breaded and deep‑fried piece of fish, usually a white‑meat variety, with lettuce, sauce, and sometimes a slice of tomato. The sandwich offers a crispy fish coating, a tender bun, and a balanced flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fish sandwich appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a quick lunch for workers.
Traditionally cod or haddock are used, but regional versions feature salmon, sea bass, or pollock.
The breading is often a mix of breadcrumbs and spices such as paprika, garlic, and black pepper.
A white bun provides a neutral backdrop that lets the sauce and fish flavor shine.
In some countries the sandwich is served with lemon wedges and tartar sauce.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Even after frying, fish retains some omega‑3s, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of bun carbohydrates and fish fats gives a quick source of energy.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High fat from frying
items.content: Frying adds saturated and trans fats, so the sandwich should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt in the breading and sauce can raise blood pressure in sensitive people.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Certain fish species may contain mercury or other heavy metals; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat with hands, but you can halve it and add fresh veggies like cucumber, radish, or lettuce. It pairs well with potato chips or a light side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. For longer storage, store the fish separately in the fridge and keep the bun in a dry place.
